reason: P1 substituted cup 2 for the requested mug, heated it, then wasted the remaining budget on repeated microwave move/open/close actions and never placed anything in the coffeemachine. P5 and P7 looped among already-inspected empty shelves/drawers, ended at the step limit, and P7 did not pursue a second keychain after placing one. By contrast, P2/P3/P4 show a working heat-then-place pattern, P6/P8/P9 complete multi-instance placements, and P10 succeeds cleanly with the desklamp. The Parent Skill has no microwave-heating sequence and only generic search guidance that does not address finding/placing a required count of instances.

plan.goal: Improve heat-then-place tasks by acquiring the exact target, using a minimal microwave heat interaction, and delivering immediately; improve multi-instance find-and-place tasks by sweeping all receptacle types once, continuing after each placement, and reaching the required count. Preserve the successful desklamp inspection sequence, successful heat-to-destination deliveries, and successful multi-instance placements.

updates.text: For any task that requires a heated object to be placed (e.g., 'hot X' or 'heat some X and put it ...'): (1) Acquire the exact named target category; do not pick up a visually similar but different category (such as a cup when a mug is requested) and, if the exact target is not yet visible, continue the systematic search instead of settling for a substitute. (2) Carry it to the microwave; if the microwave is closed, open it once. (3) With the target held at the open microwave, issue exactly one 'heat <target> with microwave 1' action. Do not repeatedly move the target into and out of the microwave and do not loop open/close actions; those steps are wasted and can consume the step budget. (4) Immediately after the successful heat action, go to the requested destination, open it if closed, and place the target there. Do not wander to unrelated cabinets or return to the microwave. (5) Stop once the heated target has been placed.

For any task requiring more than one instance of a target category ('two X', 'find two X', etc.): (1) Treat the initial room listing as the search set and inspect each receptacle type at least once: open every closed cabinet, drawer, and fridge encountered, and also check open furniture surfaces such as countertops, diningtables, coffeetables, shelves, dressers, beds, sofas, sidetables, tvstands, armchairs, and desks; do not restrict the sweep to one furniture type (for example, only shelves and drawers) while other listed receptacles remain unchecked. (2) When a location is visibly empty or an object there has already been moved, go to a different not-yet-inspected receptacle rather than immediately re-checking the same empty container; do not cycle among a small set of already-inspected locations. (3) After delivering one instance to the destination, resume the sweep for the next instance from unvisited receptacles instead of stopping at one or rechecking emptied ones. (4) Continue until the requested number of instances of the exact category has been placed; do not substitute another category to reach the count. (5) Stop once the required count is placed.

checks.question: On a heat-then-place task, does the Actor acquire the exact named category, perform the heat action with at most minimal microwave door manipulation, and then go directly to the requested destination and place the heated target?
Does the Actor avoid repeated microwave move/open/close cycles and avoid leaving the microwave area without delivering the heated object?

On a task requiring two or more instances, does the Actor continue into previously uninspected receptacle types after placing one instance, rather than rechecking already-empty locations, and does it place the full requested count?
Do the successful desklamp-inspection behavior and straightforward successful transfer/placement behaviors remain intact without unnecessary heating detours?
